title: Introduce telemetry-driven batch/cache defaults and model quantization recommender
author: Aisha Patel
body:
Motivation and summary:
This PR adds a small, opinionated subsystem that derives safer out-of-the-box batching and cache TTL defaults from live telemetry, plus a lightweight per-model quantization recommendation engine. The intention is to reduce unit inference cost for newly onboarded models and routes while preserving tail-latency SLOs. The feature is conservative: it only suggests defaults (not forced changes), is rollable via feature flag, and emits extensive metrics for validation.

What changed (high level):
- A telemetry aggregator (telemetry/collector) that computes request-size and inter-arrival percentiles and produces a compact profile for each route/model.
- A policy module (runtimes/batcher/policy.py + go shim) that converts profiles into batching targets, max batch windows, and cache TTL hints using heuristics tuned for 95th/99th latency control.
- A quantization recommender (tools/quant/recommender.py) that suggests FP16, int8 or int8-q4 variants based on model architecture tag, observed token lengths, and quality-sensitivity signals (failure-rate proxy).
- Console/Console metrics and docs: new telemetry metrics, a small UI hint hook, and a runbook describing safe rollout.

Why this is different from previous autotuners in the repo:
- Focus on live-telemetry-derived defaults instead of aggressive autotuning during serving. We want safe starter defaults so customers see immediate cost wins without risking instability from online parameter changes.
- The quant recommender is model-aware and conservative: recommendations include an expected quality-impact score and a suggested evaluation prompt set.

Design notes and algorithms (short):
- Batching defaults: compute p50/p90/p99 of tokens-per-request and arrival gap. For routes with p99 latencies > target, suggest reducing max batch window and lowering target batch size; for low-latency routes with high parallelism, recommend larger batch targets. We prefer floor/ceil clamp ranges to avoid pathological choices.
- Cache TTL estimator: uses request-key reuse rate and a discounted hit-value heuristic (expected tokens saved / added latency). TTL = min(max_ttl, f(reuse_rate, cost_per_token, latency_sensitivity)).
- Quant recommender: score = alpha*model_size_factor + beta*median_tokens + gamma*failure_rate_proxy. Thresholds tuned to minimize expected quality loss while maximizing per-token savings. Suggestions are accompanied by an eval plan and a simulated throughput/cost delta.

Checklist / PR scope:
- [x] Telemetry collector and compact profile producer
- [x] Policy translator for batch/cache defaults
- [x] Quant recommender and CLI summary command
- [x] Unit tests for core heuristics (python/go)
- [x] Integration smoketest that runs against local perf harness with synthetic traces
- [x] Console metrics + runbook doc
- [x] Feature flag gated rollout with canary percent param

Testing and validation:
- Unit tests: added for scoring functions and TTL math (pytest).
- Integration: a small harness run simulated three workload shapes (chatty short reqs, medium-balanced, long-streaming) and asserts that the suggested defaults did not raise 99th latency by more than 5% in the synthetic environment while reducing estimated per-token cost by 9-23% depending on workload.
- Staging rollout: deployed behind feature flag targeting 3% of traffic for 24h with realtime dashboards. No regressed alerts during canary.

Files changed (summary):
- runtimes/batcher/policy.py: new heuristic translator and config serializer
- runtimes/batcher/telemetry_collector.go: Go sidecar to read aggregated metrics and publish compact profiles
- platform/telemetry/metrics_schema.yaml: new metrics for profile exports and recommendation confidence
- tools/quant/recommender.py: recommendation engine + cli
- console/hooks/cost-hints.tsx: small UI hint that surfaces suggestions in model settings
- docs/runbook/cost-defaults.md: rollout and rollback playbook
- tests/integration/test_defaults_smoke.py: synthetic workload tests
- tools/quant/fixtures/sample_profiles.json: sample profiles used by tests
- platform/feature_flags/config.yaml: flag gate for the feature

Commits (high level):
- 1a2b3c4: initial telemetry schema and collector shim
- 2b3c4d5: batcher policy and heuristic functions
- 3c4d5e6: quant recommender implementation + CLI
- 4d5e6f7: tests + integration harness updates
- 5e6f7g8: docs, console hook, and feature flag wiring

Review conversation (high level):
- Marco Diaz (reviewer): "Nice separation between producer and policy. Two asks: make TTL formula more explicit in comments; add a guard for zero-division in the score."
  - Author response: "Added inline doc for TTL formula and explicit safe-guards; also included a reference test case for zero reuse-rate."
- Ruth Kim (reviewer): "Concerned about the quant recommender thresholds for transformer-decoder models — can we make thresholds configurable per family?"
  - Author response: "Made family overrides configurable and added a small mapping for the open models we ship by default. Defaults retain conservative behavior."
- Jonas Müller (approver): "Bench runs look good; ensure the UI hint is toggleable by orgs that opt out."
  - Author response: "Added org-level opt-out flag and a console permission check."

CI and checks summary:
- unit-tests: pass
- integration-smoke: pass (ran in ~14m)
- lint: pass (python+ts+go linters)
- flow/static-analysis: pass
- e2e: skipped (feature-flag gated)
- deployments/staging: pass

Files changed count: 9
Additions: 1283
Deletions: 412

Deployment and rollout plan:
- Feature flag default: off.
- Stage 0 (canary): enable for 3% of routed traffic in staging for 24h, observe metrics.
- Stage 1: enable for 5% of production traffic; hold 48h; watch 99th latency, error-rate, and recommendation acceptance by customers.
- Stage 2: incrementally increase to 25% if metrics stable.
- If any regression >8% p99 latency or uptick in customer facing errors, auto-roll back via the flag.

Release notes (user-facing):
- Adds telemetry-driven "Suggested defaults" for batching and cache TTL in the Console. Suggestions include an expected cost delta and a recommended eval plan.
- Adds a conservative model quantization recommender that proposes quant formats with an accompanying quality-impact estimate.

Risk and mitigations:
- Risk: overly aggressive defaults causing latency regressions. Mitigation: conservative thresholds, clamp ranges, and feature-flag gated rollout with canary.
- Risk: noisy telemetry leading to bad suggestions. Mitigation: compact profile uses 24h window and percentile smoothing; we include a confidence score and only surface high-confidence suggestions by default.

Post-merge actions:
- Run an A/B with live traffic for 2 weeks, collect acceptance rate of recommendations and measured cost delta.
- Add an alert rule to flag large disagreement between simulated cost-savings and realized savings (>25%).

Merge outcome:
- Merged via squash-merge after approvals from two reviewers and green CI.
